1.why: All nine screenshots show a static, uncluttered card-based layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings, high-contrast teal primary buttons, and shaded info/reminder boxes make key elements stand out on every step.

3.why: Each screen has a single clear title and main action in a linear flow, though the persistent logs panel adds minor visual noise.

4.why: The user must remember multi-part password rules (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol) plus handle sequential recovery and MFA codes.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill affordances, or “remember me” controls appear in any screenshot.

6.why: Fields are blank or only once pre-filled with a recovery identifier; no saved-account chips or familiar-item recognition aids are shown.

7.why: Labels and most instructions are concise and readable, although a few reminder paragraphs run longer.

8.why: No error messages are present in any of the nine screenshots, so the claim that they describe problems and fixes cannot be verified.

9.why: Password rules and code length are stated, but no concrete typed examples (e.g., sample password or format illustration) are provided.

10.why: Only a fixed password-then-MFA-code sequence is offered; no clear alternative choices such as face login are presented.

11.why: Every screen limits the user to at most two prominent actions, avoiding simultaneous choice overload.

12.why: Explicit outcome text appears after actions (e.g., “secure instructions have been prepared”, “Your appointment request has been confirmed”) plus updating logs.

13.why: Safe-sign-in callouts and password-requirement tips supply short guidance on multiple steps.

14.why: Visible “Start over”, “Return to sign in”, and “Forgot password?” buttons let the user retry after mistakes.

15.why: Identical header, card structure, button styles, logs panel, and footer warning persist across all nine steps.
